meta.title: Why You Absolutely Hate Your Own Voice #shorts
meta.description:
Have you ever listened to a recording of your own voice and immediately wanted to crawl into a hole? You are definitely not alone. When you speak, you actually hear your voice in two different ways at the exact same time. First, the sound waves travel through the air into your ears. But second, the sound also vibrates through your skull bones, which artificially deepens the tone and makes it sound much richer to you. When you hear a recording, you only hear the air-conducted sound, which makes your voice sound surprisingly high-pitched and unfamiliar. Your brain experiences a weird cognitive dissonance because it expects one sound but gets another. It literally tricks you into feeling cringed out by your own natural pitch. Do you actually like your voice? Hit follow for more mind-blowing facts!
